title: Wrong icon shown when launching same app twice via two different .desktop files that have different icons
line: An app started from a second desktop file with its own icon now gets its own task with that icon instead of joining the app's usual task.
explanation: The task manager maps a window to a desktop file from the window's own metadata, matching its app id first. Two desktop files that start the same program (for example Thunderbird with two profiles, or a second launcher with other arguments and icon) give windows with the same app id, so both always mapped to the program's own desktop file, icon and task. Now, when KIO launched the process in its own systemd unit (app-<desktop file>-<uuid>.scope or app-<desktop file>@<uuid>.service), that desktop file is preferred, as long as it runs the same executable and doesn't declare a StartupWMClass for some other window.

commits.message:
libtaskmanager: use the desktop file a window was launched from

When two desktop files start the same program, its windows share an app
id, so they were always mapped to the program's own desktop file and
icon. Now prefer the desktop file in the process's systemd launch unit.

BUG: 475736

media.caption: Dolphin started from its own desktop file and from a second 'Home Folder Browser' file with a game icon: both windows land in the one Dolphin task
Same steps with the fix: the second window gets its own task with the second file's icon

review.text: The idea (prefer the desktop file named in KIO's systemd launch unit, guarded by same executable and StartupWMClass) is reasonable, but it was written and tested on the pre-47b52acb serviceFromMetadata. On current origin/master the hunk 'applies cleanly' only because it matches the final servicesFromPid fallback, so the check now runs only in the last-chance PID path and never for windows whose appId matches a desktop file, i.e. the reported case is not fixed on master.
changes: Rebase properly onto 47b52acb: apply the launch-scope preference right after the appId desktopEntryName match (and ideally the StartupWMClass matches) in the new serviceFromMetadata, not in the servicesFromPid fallback.
Re-verify the Dolphin/second-desktop-file repro on current master and add a tasktoolstest case if feasible.
